name: Child's Pose
description: Child's pose is a resting yoga posture that places the spine in a supported flexed position and gently stretches the latissimus dorsi, thoracic extensors, and hip flexors simultaneously. The extended arm variation provides a substantial lat stretch while the kneeling position creates mild hip flexor lengthening. It is used widely as a recovery position, a breathing exercise, and a preparatory or finishing movement in mobility routines.

execution.starting_position: Kneel on the floor with knees wide and toes touching. Sit the hips back toward the heels.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a mat for comfort. If the hips do not reach the heels, place a folded blanket between the thighs and calves.
steps: Step 1: Kneel on the floor with knees wider than hip-width and toes together.
Step 2: Sit the hips back toward the heels.
Step 3: Extend both arms forward on the floor as far as possible, lowering the chest toward the floor.
Step 4: Rest the forehead on the floor or a cushion.
Step 5: Hold 60–120 seconds, breathing deeply into the back body.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe deeply. On each inhale, feel the ribcage expand sideways and upward. On each exhale, allow the body to sink more completely into the position.
common_mistakes: Keeping the knees together, which limits hip comfort — wider knees are more accommodating for most people
Not allowing the arms to extend fully overhead, limiting the lat stretch
Tensing the neck — allow the head to rest completely
safety_considerations: If knee discomfort is present, place padding under the knees or avoid if severe
Those with ankle mobility limitations may need a rolled towel under the ankles
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Extend the arms as far forward as comfortable and allow the forehead to rest on the floor.
coaching_cues: Let gravity do the work — just breathe and release
Walk your fingers further away from your body on each exhale
Allow the shoulder blades to spread apart
